title: feat: add app screenshot URL contract
author: ElliotEtag
pr_body_excerpt:
- Adds an optional, validated `screenshotUrl` field to `apps/catalog.json`; URLs must be non-root, whitespace-free `media.pollinations.ai` object URLs.
- Carries the field through the Tinybird app directory datasource, sync job, and public endpoint.
- Seeds seven unique screenshots across eight matching catalog rows and restores CatGPT’s live URL/platform.
- Keeps existing catalog entries and consumers compatible when no screenshot is present.

Checks:
- Catalog validation and all app tests
- Biome
- Tinybird definition parsing
- HTTP 200 + `image/webp` for all eight uploads

Deployment:
- Tinybird definitions are deployed and verified in staging and production.
- Merging this PR triggers the catalog sync; dispatch it manually only if that run does not complete.
- The website consumer is the immediate follow-up.

Retention:
- Media objects expire after 30 days and organic traffic is not the retention strategy.
- Website-v2 already deduplicates catalog rows by name.
- A separate scheduled screenshot job will recapture/re-upload on a roughly 15-day cadence and must land before the initial uploads expire in early September.

gist.headline: The app garden gets portraits
gist.blurb: The app directory can now carry little window-views of what people are building. Seven apps have already sat still long enough for a screenshot, which is unusually cooperative behavior for software.
gist.summary: Added an optional validated screenshotUrl contract to apps/catalog.json, syncing non-root media.pollinations.ai object URLs through the Tinybird app-directory datasource and public endpoint, with seven screenshots seeded across eight catalog rows.
gist.impact: Directory consumers can now display verified WebP app screenshots when available while existing catalog entries remain fully compatible without a screenshotUrl.
gist.visual_concept: Depict the app directory as a cozy greenhouse gallery: small retro CRT frames show distinct app screenshots growing among labeled code-plants. Polli, wearing a tiny curator beret, carefully hangs a fresh screenshot in a frame while the eager monitor robot admires the organized collection; the visual metaphor is that catalog entries have gained reliable visual portraits.

Polli is a cute pixel art bee mascot with a yellow body and dark brown horizontal stripes, small black legs, two black antennae, black vertical oval eyes, bright pink rectangular blush marks on cheeks, a small happy smile, and small rounded light blue translucent wings; she wears a tiny curator beret and hangs a new screenshot frame beside an eager chunky monitor robot.
